- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day post-spike.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–7 days.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) — adjust for lagged sentiment shifts by adding 0.2–0.8% to forecast if sentiment turns positive.
- For 10+ day horizons, model often underestimates volatility; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast if sentiment is mixed or trending upward.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high/low cycles, model fails to capture momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 3–5 days to adjust forecast midpoint.
